title: Wikipedians Believed AI Would Come and Go. They Were Wrong
source_used: WIRED, book excerpt by Richard Cooke (full text read)
key_facts: WIRED published an excerpt from Richard Cooke's book 'The Last Best Place on the Internet: A Human History of Wikipedia' (W. W. Norton, 2026).

A Princeton University study found about 5 percent of nearly 3,000 newly created English Wikipedia articles in August 2024 contained a substantial amount of AI-generated content (as cited by Cooke, who dates the study October 2024).

By March 2026, AI content so often broke Wikipedia's core principles that writing with large language models was banned outright, with their role restricted to translation and minor proofreading (Cooke's account).
Pew Research counted 1.9 trillion Wikipedia views between 2015 and 2025, about 508 million a day.

Long-time Wikipedian Christophe Henner, in a January 2026 'wake-up call', wrote that since 2022 the encyclopedia had lost almost a quarter of its readership, more than 1.1 billion visits a month, and that click-through from AI chatbots was 0.33 percent versus about 9 percent for Google search.
Henner also called AI 'an accelerant, not the fire', pointing to a generational shift from reading articles to scrolling fragments, and warned of an editing crisis with fewer editors doing more work.
Cooke notes that Google's AI Overviews became as central to the search experience as Wikipedia once was, and that AI agents give plausible but often wrong answers.
Most of the excerpt is essay and history (H. G. Wells, Enlightenment encyclopedias, Wikimania), not news.
quote_evidence: By March 2026, AI content was found to violate its core principles so often that writing with large language models was banned outright, and their role restricted to translation and minor proofreading.
Since 2022, the encyclopedia had lost almost a quarter of its readership, more than 1.1 billion visits per month, a missing audience who, presumably, were seeking out AI summaries instead.
AI is an accelerant, not the fire.
why_it_matters_hint: A widely read free reference is losing readers and volunteers as AI answers spread, and has banned AI-written text.
event_date: Excerpt published 13 Oct 2026; events it recounts: Aug 2024 study, Jan 2026 Henner warning, Mar 2026 ban
notes: A book excerpt of essay length, not a news report; the facts it recounts date from 2024 to March 2026 with no new event on 13 Oct, so the score is lowered by 1. The ban's scope is Cooke's account; no Wikimedia statement was read.
